getLawyer.why: If you are arrested or detained in France, ask for a lawyer and for the Canadian consular office to be notified (Embassy of Canada (Paris): +33 (0)1 44 43 29 02). Sign nothing you do not understand. Dual citizenship is legally recognized; Canadian consular services may be limited and different entry/exit rules may apply.

Penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs in France are severe — jail or heavy fines. Contact the Canadian consular office and get a local lawyer; say and sign nothing without counsel.

deadlines.title: Schengen 90/180 — max 90 days in any 180
deadlines.rule: Canadians need no visa for up to 90 DAYS in any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen area. Your passport must be valid at least 3 MONTHS beyond the date you expect to leave the Schengen area. The Entry/Exit System (EES) records biometric data on arrival; ETIAS will be required once it opens — apply only on the official EU website. Dual citizens of a participating country must travel on their European passport.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — France

deadlines.title: Drive up to 1 year on a Canadian licence
deadlines.rule: A valid Canadian licence is accepted for the first YEAR; longer stays require exchanging it for a French licence. Minimum driving age 18. A reflective vest and warning triangle are required in all vehicles; winter tires or chains are compulsory in some mountain areas from November 1 to March 31.
deadlines.source: Government of Canada travel advice — France

statutes.title: Identification
statutes.summary: Carry valid ID such as a driver's licence or passport, or a copy; keep photocopies or digital copies stored separately.

book.title: Police, ID, and if you're detained in France
book.overview: Carry valid ID such as a driver's licence or passport, or a copy; keep photocopies or digital copies stored separately. If you are arrested or detained, ask for a lawyer and ask that the Canadian consular office be told. Emergency: 112 (police direct: 17). Dual citizenship is legally recognized; Canadian consular services may be limited and different entry/exit rules may apply.
your_rights: Ask for a lawyer before answering questions.
Ask the authorities to notify the Canadian consular office.
Ask for an interpreter if you do not understand the language.
Do not sign anything you do not understand.
key_steps: Carry ID (or a copy) as the local rules require.
If detained: ask for a lawyer, an interpreter, and the Canadian consular office.
Save the emergency number (112 (police direct: 17)) and the consular contact (+33 (0)1 44 43 29 02).
Report theft to the police to get a report for insurance.
common_mistakes: Not carrying ID or a copy.
Assuming dual citizenship guarantees Canadian consular help.
book.when_lawyer: Immediately on arrest or detention — ask for a lawyer and the Canadian consular office.

book.title: Local laws that catch visitors in France
book.overview: Penalties for possession, use or trafficking of illegal drugs are severe — convicted offenders can expect jail sentences or heavy fines. Other local rules that surprise visitors: It is illegal to cover your face in public places, including airport arrivals areas — fines apply, with no exemption for tourists or for religious reasons. Drones must be registered before flying; violations risk a fine or imprisonment. Smoking is banned in woods and forests during high fire-risk periods, including within 200 m of wooded areas.
your_rights: The right to a lawyer if you are charged.
The right to have the Canadian consular office notified.
The right to an interpreter in proceedings you do not understand.
key_steps: Do not carry packages or luggage for anyone else.
Learn the local rules below before you go — ignorance is not a defence.
It is illegal to cover your face in public places, including airport arrivals areas — fines apply, with no exemption for tourists or for religious reasons.
Drones must be registered before flying; violations risk a fine or imprisonment.
common_mistakes: Assuming rules are the same as in Canada.
Carrying or using drugs because they seem tolerated locally.
book.when_lawyer: As soon as you are questioned about, or charged with, any offence.

book.title: Crime, scams and driving in France
book.overview: Pickpocketing and bag or phone snatching are frequent, especially on public transport and in tourist areas, often using distraction; illegal taxis at Paris airports and stations overcharge tourists. Driving: A valid Canadian licence is accepted for the first YEAR; longer stays require exchanging it for a French licence. Minimum driving age 18. A reflective vest and warning triangle are required in all vehicles; winter tires or chains are compulsory in some mountain areas from November 1 to March 31.
your_rights: To report a crime to the police and receive a report for insurance.
To consular assistance from Canada if you are a victim of crime.
To drive on your Canadian licence for the period stated, if you meet the conditions.
key_steps: Keep valuables out of sight and bags closed in crowds and on transit.
Use only licensed taxis and check ATMs before using your card.
Carry the required safety equipment and documents when driving.
Report theft promptly and contact your card issuer.
common_mistakes: Leaving valuables in a parked car.
Driving without the required permit, equipment, or insurance.
Ignoring local traffic-zone and alcohol rules.
book.when_lawyer: After a serious collision, any arrest, or a significant theft or fraud.
